statement: The first line holds n; the second holds n integers, negatives allowed. Print the length of the largest contiguous subarray whose sum is 0, or 0 when none exists. This is the sum-k problem at k equals 0, with the cleanest possible signal: a zero-sum stretch exists exactly where a prefix value repeats, because equal markers mean the gap between them cancelled. Map each prefix value to its first index (seed 0 at -1) and measure the gap whenever a repeat appears.

example.why: Prefix 9 appears at index 0 and again at index 5 - the five elements between cancel to 0.

hint: Repeated prefix value equals zero-sum gap; first sighting fixed, latest repeat measured.
mistake: Updating the stored index on every repeat - the map must keep the earliest, or spans shrink.
